title: Complete summary – The breast
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture. 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

Which technique, when 🔁🔁

TechniqueIndications
Mammographyscreening from 40–50 y, first step > 50 y, follow-up after breast cancer; two views craniocaudal + mediolateral oblique; best for microcalcifications; limited in dense breasts
Ultrasoundwomen < 30 y (first exam for a lump), dense breast, cyst vs solid, biopsy guidance; many sonographic patterns; not only for suspected malignancy
MRIhigh-risk (BRCA) screening, implants, extent/multifocality, response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy – complementary, not first line
CTmediastinal nodes / distant staging
  • Mammography is NOT the only method used.

Benign vs malignant 🔁

BenignMalignant
Simple cyst (anechoic, posterior enhancement); oval circumscribed mass parallel to the skin; coarse popcorn calcification (fibroadenoma); fat-containing lesionSpiculated / angular / indistinct margins; taller-than-wide; posterior shadowing; fine linear branching microcalcifications; architectural distortion; skin thickening & nipple/skin retraction

BI-RADS 🔁

ScoreMeaning / action
0incomplete – more imaging
1–2negative / benign
3probably benign (< 2 %) – short-interval follow-up
4, 5suspicious / highly suggestive → BIOPSY
6already biopsy-proven cancer (no new biopsy)
